body.statement: Along the retained even tail \(n\ge N_0\), the terminal covariate limit satisfies the following distinction. For every finite \(a>0\), the terminal covariate limit \(C_{k,a}\) is not equal in distribution to the classical uniform-rerandomization limit \(L_{k,a}\): the former assigns mass \(1-\Pr(\chi_k^2\le a)\) to the sphere \(\{d:\|d\|^2=a\}\), whereas the latter assigns that sphere probability zero.
body.justification: A boundary-atom certificate prevents the original first-entry output from being silently replaced by a uniform acceptable-set draw.
body.gap: Li, Ding, and Rubin characterize uniform Mahalanobis rerandomization, while Lu, Zhang, and Zhu restore that uniform law only after changing the algorithm.
body.consumer: Analysts can diagnose exactly why truncated-Gaussian reference intervals are not calibrated for uncorrected first-entry PSRR.
